what: every job sent to the lab carried the same lines again - how to stop, to enter, to stand, to land - and, to change a few lines of a program, the whole of each file changed: one job carried 63 thousand bytes, 50 thousand of them files sent whole. And what was got right by care was got wrong by hand: a summary too long to be a title five times in two days, a comparison moved by the work itself five times. The lens of work done by hand shows it as the handwork recorded most: patching source code by matching text

oco-agent exists only as built on the lab: lab-agent's releases do not carry it, so a driver elsewhere has it by the lab's hand. Looked at before replacing (2026-11-14): it is not an oversight - release-plz.toml says oco-agent grows here beside lab-agent and is not released until it takes over. What it waits on is the switch: the daemon retiring, which waits on the author's own driving

countermeasure: oco-agent's crates given their own tag names (PR 156); still open within it: a failing run after a merge must be heard (backlog:release-runs-watched) And now heard: the lab says a run that fails on main within a quarter hour, and the picture shows it (working the-lab-hears-what-fails).
what: 21 release runs failed after oco-agent's crates joined the workspace, and nothing said so

countermeasure: listings read from the git tree, a cut-short listing refused, every request with time limits (lab-agent 0.1.53)
what: lab-agent replayed finished jobs: GitHub's directory listing stops at 1,000 entries without saying so

A driver elsewhere got to the lab one way: the private jobs repository, written through GitHub's API with the lab's own token copied into a sandbox that is not kept. Nothing in the ecosystem said how a driver gets to the lab. On 2026-11-15 the driver's workspace was replaced by one whose way out attaches its own credential, repository by repository, and passes reads and pushes only. The token reached nothing; an asking could not be written; a beat could not be said, the repository's Actions being closed there. For most of an hour nothing could be asked of the lab, though nothing of ours had changed, and the lab went on observing by itself.

countermeasure: every git address on the lab is plain (the credential helper reaches GitHub without a secret in the address) and each was proven to reach GitHub so; the log is masked on the lab; the search now covers every git address and the usual credential and shell files. The log's earlier form stays in the private jobs repository's history: revoking the old token is what ends it.
what: ten repositories on the lab carried the old token in their git settings - nine in a remote address, one as the address a branch pushes to, so it was still in use - while it had been said that nothing on the lab held it: only two folders had been searched, and the claim was wider than the check. Looking printed it into a job's log
the GitHub token can do far more than the lab needs - delete repositories, administer organizations and the enterprise - so whoever holds it can do all of that

countermeasure: rotated 2026-11-12 by the author. The new token reached the lab sealed with a one-time key made on the lab (RSA-OAEP), never in the jobs repository; installed in its two places (token, env), the voice and oco-agent restarted onto it, and the work landed through it. The assistant's helpers read it from a private file, no longer written into commands. The old token is kept aside, private, until the author revokes it. Corrected 2026-11-13: it was not true that nothing on the lab held the old token - ten git addresses did (problem the-old-token-in-git-addresses). They are plain now, and the old token can be revoked. 2026-11-13: every git setting on the lab is plain; the old token is no longer used anywhere on the lab.
what: the GitHub token appeared in process listings and in conversation; it must be rotated

Which lenses the voice follows - work and signs - is written in the voice's script on the lab, not said by a lens: what is said aloud to the author where he is, is a lens of lenses like what a place shows first, and it is kept outside the language. So what followed a thing he said - each record of work as it lands, each release - does not reach his phone; and the voice hears of a landing only when the observatory next observes the whole, four times a day.

countermeasure: the pulse at Healthchecks is the lab's watcher; the workflow is a probe run by hand (decisions:2026-11-12-the-pulse-is-the-watcher). Its alerts reach the author's email; through ntfy once the author adds that integration in Healthchecks.
what: the watcher's schedule ran once, nine hours late, then not again: GitHub's schedules are best-effort and drop silently

The words every job uses are a copy the lab keeps beside the place that holds them, and what landed in that place was not in use until a job put it there by a line of its own. The job that landed a new way to carry what is said in the window had no such line: the next saying was carried by the words from before, and what it entered in a second place stayed unlanded until a job landed it.

entered on 2026-11-14 as: oco-agent wait did not see a long job end. Looked into the same day, it is not so: each of the jobs ran longer than the time the wait was given - 322, 581, 316 and 420 seconds, against 290 to 298 - and the wait was still waiting, rightly, when it was cut off by the one who asked. Kept as it was said and what the journal says of it; see open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, reflection 2026-11-14-a-sign-written-from-an-impression

countermeasure: Withdrawn 2026-11-13: it was raised on a misreading. readiness is the milestone's rung on the path - this one is the ninth - not how much of it is done; it is rightly not reached, because the item it rests on (rhizcut) is open. The record was right. What remains true is only that: the tool that takes a cutting is not built.
what: the milestone rhizoid-carries-ocoeco (ocoeco travels as a rhizcut) stands at 9 of 9, while its only criterion is the item rhizcut - open, and written down only on 2026-11-12 because the milestone pointed at nothing; the tool is not on the lab and has no repository

countermeasure: the docs begin their own history (decisions:2026-11-12-the-docs-own-history): manifest at 0.0.0 read by release-please, versions below 1.0 while forming, the template's changelog cleared with a note
what: the release pull request proposes 1.0.0 while the manifest says 1.2.0: no release was ever tagged, so release-please starts from nothing

countermeasure: allowed for this repository, default permissions kept read-only; the release run succeeded and opened its pull request
what: the docs release failed on every merge for two days, 54 times, unheard: Actions were not permitted to open pull requests in the phone organization

the lenses built into ocoeco are not things: one cannot stand on a lens and look around - what it reads, what places it, what asks of its shapes - as on anything else; only the lens of language sees them, as rows of its own

a next step is words, and whether it has been taken cannot be read off: read as work recorded after it was said, it showed a step as passed minutes after it was said, for working toward a step is not the step done. Were it a link to what is to be done - as waiting became a link to what halts - its being done would be read off. Until then it is the one typed thing on an item that ages unseen; 12 of 332 items say one. And a row cannot be taken back through an entry: the part that showed this was taken out of a file by hand
an item's next step is typed, and goes stale as a typed state did: a lens that makes lenses said its next was a trial made two days before, at the head of a line of halting five long

a place is found, when observing, by a label put on its repository by hand (the topic oco-project), through GitHub's search - which lags behind what exists; its mark already says it is a place, and an observatory already says what it gathers (every star of an owner). The conversation, made a place on 2026-11-14 under an owner the author's observatory gathers, was not observed until it was given the label

A release is made, and its files are built after it: for some minutes the newest release of a program has nothing to take, and whoever takes the newest finds nothing. On 2026-11-15 the author's observatory, asked to observe a minute after ocoeco 0.49.0 was released, failed on main. It now takes the newest release that has its files; but the gap is of every program released this way - the release made by release-please, its files by the conveyor later in the same run - and each who takes one would have to know of it. A release said only once it can be taken would have no gap.

a place may say the shape of what it keeps in a declaration of its own - the canon's tables.toml, which its own check holds every row to - and the ecosystem's entries do not read it: an entry can ask only for a field a lens declares. So a field on such a row is written with note, past the entries, or its table is declared a second time in a lens. One nature - what a table is - said in two places that do not know of each other

a star's idea - why it exists, in its own words, 95 rows across the stars - is pointed at by nothing, and a walk arrives at the one line its mark says instead: what a star is for is said twice, and the fuller saying is not reached

four of the observatory's practices still say how work was done through lab-agent - its guide at the start of a session, its inbox, its board, its jobs - where oco-agent now runs the work and the board is read off what was done

all 20 principles and all 10 architectures of the canon are pointed at by nothing: what is said to govern how things are made is followed, or not, without anything saying where. The observatory's practices now say where they are shown - eight of 36 - by a relation any place's lens may declare; the canon's do not yet

what a route reads - a commit, a guard, a file of source - is a row a lens can ask of, and not a thing in the graph: one cannot stand on a guard, and a decision cannot point at the guard that holds it, nor a record of work at the change git has for it. And a route is read only where a place is held: from what an observatory observed - as a published page is built - there is no history, no source, no guards

countermeasure: ocoeco check brings every lens into focus over the place, so a lens that cannot is not landed; jobs run with pipefail, so a piped command's failure stops them
what: the problems lens landed with a focus that could not run (a reserved word unquoted); the job printed the error and carried on, its failure hidden by a pipe

What git says of when a change was made is kept in the clock of whoever made it - 2026-11-15T00:08:46+01:00 - while every record of work, run and turn says its moment in UTC. Read as words the two do not line up: on 2026-11-15 at 19:46 UTC the flow said the latest thing in view was at 20:46, and what is taken to follow a thing said would be an hour off.

ocoeco manual, asked from a job to count something done by hand - by the id of its record, with no words of the action - opened its list to choose from: a window, which a job has not. It stopped with a panic - failed to initialize terminal - and nothing said of why; twice, on 2026-11-15, counting the day's handwork, and each time the job stopped and the place was put back. Told the action in words it counts at once. What it lacked could have been said in a sentence.

the 45 conditions milestones rest on are written feature:voice-calls@linux-best, while the table is called features: one name for one place written two ways, as connection and connections. So the graph passes over all of them, and says that nothing points at any of the 46 features while 45 conditions do. Not mended by guessing that an s is missing: a name is not the place it names, and what is lacking is that the language say which names are one
date is declared a date in reflections and words in connections, decisions and research: one meaning, two kinds

A job that stands on a thing - to say where its record of work was made - or looks through a lens from a thing, steps in the driver's own trail: after it, the driver stands in the window where the job stood, not where they were. What followed, said next, was looked through from a lens and showed nothing. One trail carries two acts: where the driver looks, and where a job says it worked.

The few words the graph keeps of a thing are taken from a short list of fields - title, what, decision, term, says, question, name, text, practice, over, summary. A kind that has none of them says nothing of itself: counted in what the author's observatory observed on 2026-11-15, 553 things of 14 kinds - 127 files of source, 107 documents, 87 of activity, 71 of ci, 49 runs, 31 parts of lenses, 19 and 12 of work done by hand, 17 surfaces and others. In a look such a thing is a line with a name and no words.

countermeasure: after landing, main itself is read back; practice 25 (evidence before the word)
what: the work lens's focus was recorded as landed while main held only the record: bringing every star to main for a proof wiped the code

A lens is known by its id alone, and that id is one name across every place in view: two places that each keep a lens called site stop every look that sees both - two lenses are called site. A thing is known by its place, its table and its id; a lens is not. Met on 2026-11-15: the first observatory's lens of its pages could not be called site, because the author's observatory keeps one, and was named commons-site. A star that names a lens as another star has stops both observatories' looks, and neither star sees why.

Every lens that looks from a thing is brought around every thing, though some look from one kind of thing only - the lens of entering from an entry, what followed from a turn of the author. Around a thing took 1.9 s before the lens of entering was built in and 2.2 s after: each such lens is asked everywhere, to say nothing.

A lens that reads a table is given it only where a lens built into the program declares it. A table a place adds to the language - the conversation's turns - is passed over without a word, and the look stops with the engine's own words: Catalog Error: Table with name turns does not exist. So what a place adds, only the one lens that declares it could read, and a second lens of the same place could not be checked.

A link written by a star's shorter name - as the window writes every here and every mark, and as a person writes - was neither held nor broken: the graph looked the star up as written. Nineteen such links were not told; their far ends did not show them, and one written wrongly would have landed unseen by the check and by the lens alike. Seen when the program's rule for links and the lens's were put side by side.

after the graph is made once in a look, the check of one place still takes 4 s (it took 4.6) and the whole dome 11 s (it took 23.5); a look through signs 0.9 s. Making the graph more than once was a cost, not the cost: what the rest of the time goes to is not known - not git, asked once, and not the graph alone. It was predicted the check would fall to a third; it fell by an eighth

at holds a moment two ways: seconds since 1970 in beats, journal and said - oco-agent's record - and words of a date and time in glimpses, runs and manual_events. One meaning, two natures of value; a lens that joins them must turn one into the other. It lives in the same record as place does, and changes with it

countermeasure: init gives a place all three from its first day, with the lenses that catch them; the two places made before are given them
what: a place made by ocoeco init had no table for glimpses, decisions or problems: the first record of work there was refused (found in the author's observatory and in OCO's place, on their first day)

countermeasure: what a milestone has reached is counted from what it rests on (decisions:2026-11-13-a-milestone-is-read-off-what-it-rests-on); the rung is shown as a rung; the problem raised against Rhizoid is withdrawn there, in words
what: readiness was read as how ready a milestone is, for days, without looking up what it means: it is the milestone's rung on the path. A lens was built on the misreading - a rung drawn as a filled bar - and a problem raised against Rhizoid on it

A part of a lens is said to rest on a shape wherever the shape's name stands in what the part asks - also as a word in a comparison: the shape that names a row, which compares what was given with 'here', is shown resting on the shape here of the lens around.

A place that observes keeps its own lenses twice: as it keeps them, and as it last observed them, among what it observed. Looking from that place at what was observed, the whole is named from the first and brought into focus through the second: a lens the place has just changed is looked through as it was. Met twice on 2026-11-15 - the first observatory's face, tried before it landed, had its rows copied by hand into what was observed; and a check that the author's whole had its new name read the old one, and stopped a job whose change was right. Published pages do not show it, since each observes anew before it lays out; a trial before landing does.

two things of one nature were merged - what a surface holds became what it has, the author's word, leaving holds to mean whether a pointing holds - by changing the files a place keeps with a program outside the language: a row cannot be renamed or taken back through an entry. So each merge, the act the whole is refined by, is still made by hand outside it

a row written into a table a place's own lens defines is checked against nothing: only the lenses built into ocoeco are the declaration a row is held to, so the lens of questions made through entries would have taken any word for any field

A part of the author's sheet was taken back on 2026-11-15, and a record of work in ocoeco's place, made standing on that part, was left pointing nowhere. Taking a row back looked only at what this place's own rows point at; the check of a place looks at that place against the others, not at every place. Only the graph over the whole saw it - and the voice told the author. I read it when I read the inbox, which I had not done.

looked at live from the author's observatory, every run is in view twice - 98 rows for 49 runs: two observatories each keep what they observed of what has run, and both are in view. The beam showed it the first time it said by which route its light came

a run stopped because a newer one was asked for is shown as failing on main: seen when several landings within minutes each started an observation - the two observatories' runs read as cancelled, and the ones after them were running or had passed

tad's packing script with only the name changed was untrue for a package at the root - the rpm tool takes -p as a folder; and only the build was run before landing, not the packing: the first release carried no files

a thing is known by its place, its table and its id - without its owner. Four places are called lens, under four owners: that shorter name is then four things. Seen where a site was first laid out: 26 pages said, 23 files written - the pages of the places called lens wrote over one another, and a line about one would have led to another's page

In the window one steps by marks only: a thing known by its name - a part of a lens, a decision of last week - is reached by walking to it from what is shown, or not at all. To change a part of the lens of entering I gave its name as an id, since nothing shown led to it; from there the lens and its other parts were three steps away.

Standing on a thing - a sign, a decision, a reflection - one is shown what is around it, and the thing itself only in the few words the graph keeps of it, cut at seventy characters: on its own page the sign a-lens-is-named-once-in-the-whole reads - A lens is known by its id alone, and that id is one name across every ... - and no more. What it says in full is read only in the files of the place that keeps it. So a step down from an overview ends in a headline.

Each time something is done by hand is a row named by its moment and its record. Counted again within one second - a job counting three looks at a page, one after the other - the rows are named alike: on 2026-11-15 the first observatory kept 16 times done by hand under 3 names. A table keyed by id held one id several times, and the check of the place said: all is well: the harvest would read this repository.

The lens of entering says where a row would be kept - the place of the thing stood on - without knowing whether that place keeps rows of that kind: a connection was offered ocoeco, which keeps none, and the entry refused it only after everything was given. Which kinds a place keeps is in its mark, and no lens reads it.

A table is keyed by its id, and the check of a place does not hold it to that. On 2026-11-15 the first observatory kept 16 times done by hand under 3 names, and its check said all is well; tried the same day in a copy of the conversation's place, a decision kept twice under one id - 3 rows under 2 names - and the check said: all is well: the harvest would read this repository. Each new time done by hand is now named apart as it is written, and the rows that were named alike were told apart; that a table holds one id twice is still seen by nothing.

countermeasure: a job writes its finding from what it counted, with every star on its main; practice 25
what: all links hold was written before the check ran, and a count was taken from copies on unlanded branches

countermeasure: the writer fixed, the links mended, and ocoeco check now follows every link (decisions:2026-11-12-relations-declared)
what: ocoeco glimpse wrote milestone: for the table milestones: seven links led nowhere, unseen since the day it was built

countermeasure: every write of rows - glimpse in both forms, and note - is guarded: if it adds a link that points nowhere, the place's tables are put back as they were and the link is named
what: a record named an item that is not there (backlog:the-switch in lab-agent) and was landed: a link was checked only when the place was, not when it was written

making the graph takes about 400 ms of every look that reads it - a step of the walk takes 1.2 s, the lens of signs 0.85 - and what in it takes that is not known. Each thing it is made of, looked through as itself, takes a few hundredths of a second; one search found by reading was 170 ms and is gone. The beam says how long a table took to gather, not what within the graph did; and the lab has nothing that samples a running program

what each milestone rests on is asked in the same words by both of purpose's parts - the list of what is being reached, and the count of what is reached. It was asked twice before as well, in words different enough that the lens of language could not see it; written the same way, it is seen. What is lacking: a part cannot name a shape that other parts - or other lenses - then ask of; a projection does not yet feed a lens as data

place names two things: in oco-agent's journal and said it is a row's place in order, a number; in the graph's things it is the place a thing is held - a place, as the author means the word, with a mark. Looked at (2026-11-14): in oco-agent it is the key of both tables and runs through twelve files; it is in the lab's live record, in the record spoken to GitHub, and in what a driver elsewhere reads it with. Changing it is changing the record of the program that runs the work, and then each driver's copy of that program, in order

repeats is walked as a line, and its walk comes back to where it began: argenv-open-lists repeats ocoeco-on-argenv, which repeats argenv-open-lists. A repeat says two things are one need with different faces; that is not a direction but a group - the lens of the graph asks it as a line of one kind, as it asks led to and refines

what has run is observed twice: by the lab every quarter hour, and by the author's observatory on GitHub - two observers of one thing; both now say it the same way, through the lens of signs, so one failing run may be said twice

countermeasure: runs are observed, never gathered: each observation replaces the table whole; a test feeds earlier runs back in and sees them dropped
what: observed runs grew with each observation (45, then 135): the observatory exports what it observed, and the next observation gathered it back in and added to it

the lens of the graph shows the longest line of one kind, and where many lines are equally long - the turns of the conversation, sixteen links and more - it shows a different one each time it is looked through: an answer that is not settled, so that two looks at the same thing differ

the page was said twice: by a lens, in the language, and by 64 lines of the program with its style - and a guard existed only to hold the two equal. Markdown was a surface of the program's that nothing asked for, where a place can say one in two entries

ocoeco's repository is the source of the program and a place that brings the same lenses: when a lens changes its name, the program installed and the place disagree until the new program is installed - met when the lens of signs was landed, and the order of the job changed for it

the walk was said twice: by the lens of around, whose answers name the thing each line is about - and again by the terminal window, which kept where one stands in its own memory, and found what a line is about by matching its words against the names of things. A walk begun there ended with the window; no other surface could go on from it; and the one who works on the ecosystem most could not use it at all

To look, to step and to enter, a driver without a terminal says commands with flags it holds in its own context, reads the places' files and pages from its own workspace, and composes each act by hand: nothing presents, from where one stands, what is there and what can be done from it. Said by the author on 2026-11-15, twice within the hour: a page is only one surface a lens of lenses projects to; and the way in is to be an interface one stands in and acts from, that presents itself from itself.

nothing in the graph says when: a thing carries where it is held, its table and what it says. One can walk by what points at what, and not by what came before what; what is happening cannot be looked at as one flow; and a look ends when it has been shown. The language has the word - a table says which of its fields dates a row - and nine tables carry a moment

In the window a lens that places other lenses shows their headings and none of their lines - what it places is one step up. A lens whose whole saying is placed - what waits on the author: the sheet, seen through the lens behind it - shows a heading with a count, and no way to the six lines it counts. And a job that stands on a thing moves where the driver stands in the window: after it, what followed was looked through from a lens, and showed nothing.

through says two natures: light passing a lens's focus (the beam: rows in, so many through) and a lens placing another lens's plane or shape side by side (a part's through). Side by side and one after another - the author's two ways lenses go together - share one word

Two records of work touch lens parts that are no longer kept - still-showing/6 in the author's observatory and the-perfect-form/5 in OCO's place, gone before taking a row back looked at what points at it. Looked at through what was observed, the lens of signs says so: two links point nowhere, on both observatories' published pages. Looked at over the places held on the lab, the same lens says nothing of them, and the check every job runs before it lands - no link in view points nowhere - passes. One whole, two looks, two answers; which look passes over the links, and why, is not known.

What a lens file keeps beside its rows is outside what an entry can say: the words written above a part - the ones above the part that says what here names still say nothing of back; the taking away of a part; and a part's place among the others, by which it is known - put one before it, and what pointed at it points at another.

What an entry changes in a lens kept as a file is not among what the record of work touched: eight rows of the lens of entering were changed in one landing, and its record names only the two decisions entered with them. So what followed a turn, read off what records touched, does not show that the language itself changed.

what an observation could not read is written to a file of the same name as the table of signs - problems.json - and is overwritten by it: the observation says 3 problems, and nothing keeps what they are. Two things under one name: what observing could not read, and what does not fit, said by whoever sees it

what a run's ending means is decided in two places - the lens of signs' query, and ocoeco's own code that says aloud what fails now - and within an hour they disagreed: the lens was corrected, and the lab went on telling the author urgently that two runs failed which had only been replaced by newer ones. A third thing does nearly the same: the voice that says what newly came into view through a lens

what fits offers, for a link, the rows of the place stood in: a link into another star - a decision in OCO's place written from ocoeco - is still typed from memory, and twice in one hour such a link was refused by the guard

a relation entered in the author's observatory for the lens of the program - a lens it does not itself keep - was accepted, the check passed, and nothing read it: a place could not adjust a lens by adding to it. Found by the thing itself trying to rearrange through itself: 538 guards each carry the path of the file they are in, and nothing could say the one points at the other without changing the program

What is entered in the window lands at once, one row at a time - each a landing of its own, minutes of checks for a few words - and rows that belong to one act are not landed as one. (That a lens with no part would be stopped by the check of its place, said here before, was not so: a lens that has no part of its own yet is not asked to come into focus.)

What a record of work touched cannot be taken back: the record points at it, and a row is taken back only where nothing in view points at it. Every row that landed through the ecosystem is touched by the record of its own landing. Tried on 2026-11-15 in a copy of the conversation's place, on a part of a lens that had landed two hours before: Error: lens_parts conversation-pages/said is not taken back: 1 thing(s) in view point at it - marshall-oco/conversation/glimpses:g-20261115-203137 - and each then points nowhere. So nothing that landed can be merged away, and what is found to be of one nature with another stays beside it: discovery piles up.

Over the places held on the lab the sheet has no part for what is failing on main: what has run is brought only by observing, and a look over the places held does not have it. On 2026-11-15 a run of the author's observatory failed on main - it took ocoeco from a release whose files were not yet built - and the sheet the driver reads at the start of each turn, over the places held, did not show it; the same sheet through what was observed did. One sheet, two looks, and the nearer one sees nothing of what GitHub alone knows: what has run, what was released, what was done there.

what points nowhere is now said in two places - the check, in the program's own code, and the graph's part of the same name; the first time both were asked they agreed, 0 and 0, over every place. One meaning kept in two places

The language is read once, as the program begins: right after a part of a lens is changed in the window, the window shows that part as it was - the change is there at the next look. And a part is said to rest on a shape whose name is only a word in what it asks: the shape that names a row, which says 'here' in a comparison, is shown resting on the shape here of the lens around.

the trail kept where a driver stood and not when, and was no part of any place: the act of looking - which the author calls a flow of data in itself - was not in the flow, and what one is working on could not be read off it as it happens

countermeasure: the name set for the repository, so a rebase signs too; proven by its own event - a collision staged on the lab against a throwaway repository: the old step fails as it did, the new one rebases and lands both Then, 2026-11-12 19:40: the guard met a harder collision - the landed change had touched the same data file - and the rebase stopped on the conflict. The data is observed whole each time, and the later observation is the fresher, so on a collision the harvest's own data wins (rebase -X theirs; nothing but the harvest writes data/).
